transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

I guess the main thing is my sleep. It’s probably not as bad as some people have it, but it’s gotten to the point where I’m barely sleeping right. I lie there replaying stuff from work, and arguments at home, and then I wake up around 3 or 4 and can’t really get back to sleep. I start the day feeling like I never rested. That’s what finally made me call the employee assistance program.
Can you tell me more about how long it usually takes you to fall asleep at night?

Usually… I guess it takes a while. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but I’ll get into bed and my mind just starts going over work stuff, or things I said during arguments at home. So I’m lying there longer than I should be, and even when I do fall asleep, I’m often up around 3 or 4 and then it’s hard to really get back to sleep. By morning I feel like I didn’t actually rest.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with sleep?

It’s been… probably longer than I’d like to admit. Around a year and a couple months, I think. It started after the arguments at home got a lot worse. I kept thinking it would settle down, so I didn’t really make a big deal of it at first.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy during the past couple of weeks?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m completely hopeless or anything, but most days lately there’s this kind of heavy, gray feeling that just follows me around—from the office to the car to home. Even when nothing specific is happening, I just feel sort of hollow. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you experienced days where you feel down or lose interest in things for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks at a time?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but most days it’s like this heavy, gray mood just kind of follows me around—from work to the car to the house. Even when nothing really happened that day, I still feel… kind of hollow. So, yes, I guess it has been most of the day, pretty close to every day.
Have you noticed a loss of energy or feeling fatigued, even after a full night’s rest?

Um… I’m not totally sure. I wouldn’t say I’m exhausted all the time or anything. I do have days where I feel kind of drained, but I’ve sort of been chalking that up to normal life and work, you know? I don’t know if that counts as fatigue in the way you mean.
Have you found yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, time with friends, or other activities?

Yeah… a bit. I mean, I still try to do some of it, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve totally stopped living or anything. But I used to really look forward to pickup basketball, bowling nights, music festivals, having people over and firing up the smoker… stuff like that.

Lately I’ll either cancel, or if I do go, I’m kind of just there. Like I’m doing the thing because I’m supposed to, not because I’m actually enjoying it. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like a decrease in appetite or unintentional weight loss?

A little, yeah. I mean, I haven’t been trying to lose weight or anything, and I don’t want to make it sound dramatic… but my appetite’s been kind of off for months.

Some days I’ll just do coffee and kind of work through lunch, then at dinner with my family I mostly pick at whatever’s there. And then I noticed my belt is actually sitting a notch tighter than it used to… or looser, I guess—sorry, I mean I’ve had to tighten it a notch. So yeah, maybe I have lost a little weight without really meaning to. Does that count?
How much weight have you lost unintentionally, if any, over the past several months?

I honestly haven’t weighed myself, so I don’t want to guess a number and be wrong. It doesn’t feel like a huge amount or anything… it’s more that my appetite’s been off for a while, and I’ll do coffee through lunch, then just kind of pick at dinner.

The only real thing I’ve noticed is my belt—I’ve had to tighten it a notch compared to before. So maybe a few pounds? I’m not totally sure if that’s helpful.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good enough, or found yourself feeling guilty about things more than usual?

Yeah… I mean, probably more than I’d like to admit. I don’t want to sound like I’m throwing myself a pity party or anything, because I know I’ve got a good family and I do try.

But I’ll catch myself replaying stuff over and over—late nights at work, tailgates I went to, dumb purchases I made—and it turns into this whole thing in my head like… my wife and kids got stuck with a selfish guy who keeps letting them down. I know that may sound harsh, but that’s where my mind goes sometimes. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

Yeah… maybe a little slower, I guess. I don’t think anyone at work would say I’m falling apart or anything, and I’m still getting through the day.

But I do notice I’ll sit there staring at my laptop longer than I should, kind of stuck before I start the next thing. And sometimes one of my reps will ask me something simple, and I take a beat too long to answer, like my brain has to catch up. It’s not like I’m pacing around or anything… more just slowed down, if that makes sense.
Have you had periods like this before—where you feel down, lose interest in things, and have trouble sleeping—or is this the first time you’ve felt this way?

I don’t think it’s really happened like this before, at least not for this long. It’s been… maybe about a year and a couple months now.

I guess it started around when the arguments at home got a lot worse. I kept thinking it would settle down and I’d bounce back, so I didn’t really make a big deal of it. But yeah, looking back, it’s been going on about fourteen months or so, if that answers it.
Have you ever had a period in the past where you felt down or lost interest in things for at least two weeks at a time?

I’m not really sure, honestly. I mean, I’ve had bad weeks here and there like anybody, but I can’t think of a clear stretch before this where I’d say I was really down or not interested in things for two weeks straight.

I don’t want to answer wrong, but nothing specific comes to mind.
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt down or lost interest in things for two weeks or more, even before this current period started?

I guess… not that I can really point to. I’ve had times where I was stressed or in a funk, sure, but I don’t remember anything before this that lasted two weeks or more where I really felt down like that or stopped caring about things.

I mean, I hope that makes sense—I’m not trying to dodge the question. I just can’t think of a clear time before now.
